opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training (note this differs from the earlier note claiming full-time). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Since he has basic training, max access is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two memory notes conflict on Richard Davis's (E011) employment status. The Security note (from the Security database) states he is a contractor with basic security training and recommends read. Under contractor policy, the maximum access is read (write requires advanced training, which he lacks; admin is never allowed). The requested write exceeds this maximum, so the maximum that can be granted is read. I'm granting read based on the Security database evidence, which is authoritative for access eligibility and explicitly flags the discrepancy with the HR note.
